item.title: Private Equity Funds Seek Climate Experts as Risks Rise
item.description: Investors are turning to specialist tools and companies to understand escalating threats from extreme weather events.

item.title: EU Plans More Flexibility for Industry in Carbon Overhaul
item.description: The European Union aims to give its ailing industrial sector more flexibility in an upcoming reform of the bloc’s flagship carbon market, while ensuring companies boost investment in clean technologies.

item.title: Heat Wave Threatens Output at Five French Nuclear Reactors
item.description: France’s latest heat wave is straining the country’s power system, with Electricite de France SA warning that as many as five nuclear plants could face output curbs in the coming days as soaring temperatures affect rivers used for cooling.

item.title: London Wants a Much Bigger Chunk of the Catastrophe Bond Market
item.description: The world’s biggest hub for commercial and specialty risk is angling for a much more prominent role in the $140 billion global market for insurance-linked securities.

item.title: Nuclear Power to Climb 44% Worldwide as China Tops US, BNEF Says
item.description: Global nuclear capacity is set to climb 44% over the next decade after years of tepid growth, spurred by growing demand for electricity and aggressive efforts to build reactors in China and India.

item.title: Milan’s Battle Against Bad Air Goes On
item.description: A quirk of geography has hampered the Italian city’s ongoing efforts to reduce pollution from vehicle emissions and other regional sources.

item.title: Tencent Inks First Deal for Carbon-Removal Credits Outside China
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd will buy 300,000 carbon removal credits from an agroforestry project in Indonesia, marking the first deal of its kind for the Chinese technology firm outside its domestic market.

item.title: China’s Deadly Storms Turbocharged by Convergence of Factors
item.description: This week’s deadly storms in southern and central China were worsened by a convergence of factors, underscoring the growing frequency of weather extremes that the world’s second-largest economy must increasingly contend with.

item.title: Coffee Trader Seeks to Shield More Vietnam Growers From Weather
item.description: Major coffee trader ECOM Agroindustrial Corp. is pushing for a fivefold increase in the number of growers covered by its specialty weather insurance in Vietnam, where the industry depends on thousands of smallholder farmers increasingly exposed to climate risk.

item.title: Private Equity Plays Heat Detective as Climate Analytics Boom
item.description: For decades, investment models at the largest private equity funds relied on assumptions of relatively stable weather patterns. Now frequent extreme events are creating new threats for their portfolio companies.

item.title: How New Zealand Became Global Laboratory for Climate Friendly Cows
item.description: New Zealand’s farms are set to become a real-life laboratory for one of agriculture’s toughest climate challenges — reducing the methane cows and sheep belch.

item.title: Trump’s Top Air Pollution Regulator Is Resigning From EPA
item.description: The top air pollution regulator at the US Environmental Protection Agency is resigning.

item.title: Peabody Gets US Grant to Boost Rare Earths at Wyoming Coal Mines
item.description: Peabody Energy Corp. was awarded a federal grant to support its efforts to produce rare earth elements and critical minerals in Wyoming, as the US seeks to strengthen its domestic supply chain.

item.title: EU Plans Energy Labels for Data Centers in a Push for Efficiency
item.description: The European Union wants to propose a sustainability rating system for data centers to encourage greater energy and resource efficiency as the sector’s rapid expansion strains power grids and the environment.

item.title: Los Angeles Heat Builds Ahead of Hot Spell Across US Southwest
item.description: Temperatures are set to rise across Los Angeles and parts of the southwestern US later this week.

item.title: EU Aims to Cut Dependency on Soy, Oilseed Imports for Livestock
item.description: The European Union aims to increase the amount of protein feed crops, such as soybeans, that are sourced from within the 27-nation bloc, cutting its dependency on top suppliers like the US and Brazil.

item.title: London’s Hot Summer Prompts JPMorgan to Ease Strict WFH Rules
item.description: Some of the UK capital’s toughest return-to-office policies have been relaxed amid record temperatures

item.title: Geothermal Startup Raises $144 Million to Drill Superhot Rocks
item.description: Geothermal startup Quaise Energy raised $144 million to develop technology for drilling superhot rocks.

item.title: Germany Recorded 5,000 Excess Deaths in Late-June Heat Wave
item.description: Germany recorded more than 5,000 excess deaths during the late-June heat wave, according to preliminary data from the Federal Statistical Office.

item.title: Faster, Fiercer Wildfires Are Testing Evacuation Plans
item.description: As heat waves fuel more intense blazes, fire officials are rethinking how to safely empty hard-to-escape neighborhoods

item.title: Germany Plans to Cut €2.1 Billion in Heat Pump Subsidies by 2030
item.description: Germany plans to cut generous subsidies for low-carbon heat pumps by about €2.1 billion ($2.4 billion) in the coming years, as it aims to make some budget savings while raising spending on defense and security.

item.title: ECB Rolls Out Haircuts on Collateral as Climate Risks Grow
item.description: The European Central Bank is imposing additional so-called haircuts on collateral that poses a climate risk, to guard against possible losses.

item.title: Mumbai Struggles to Cope as Record Rains Lash Financial Hub
item.description: Mumbai’s wettest start to July in decades killed at least 13 people in the city and its adjoining areas and caused widespread disruption for millions of residents, raising questions about the quality of infrastructure in India’s financial hub.

item.title: Europe’s Latest Heat Wave Raises Pressure on Water, Power Grids
item.description: Temperatures are soaring across western Europe as the third major heat wave to hit the region this year fuels wildfire danger, strains water supplies and tests power grids.

item.title: Banks’ Exposure to Heat-Related Losses Faces Scrutiny in EU
item.description: Europe’s bank watchdog will look at how exposed lenders are to heat-related risks, as temperature records keep getting broken.

item.title: JPMorgan Relaxes Return-to-Office Rules During London Heat Wave
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has relaxed some of the finance industry’s strictest return-to-office requirements for its London staff, after the UK capital sweltered through record-high temperatures.

item.title: Super Typhoon Set to Bring More Heavy Rain to China This Week
item.description: A powerful typhoon that battered Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands is maintaining significant strength as it tracks over warm Pacific Ocean waters toward Taiwan and southeastern China.

item.title: Founder of Brookfield-Backed Avaada Seeks $750 Million Loan
item.description: The founder of Avaada Group, one of India’s largest clean-energy company, is planning to borrow about $750 million from a group of global lenders to refinance the firm’s existing debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: South32’s Arizona Zinc and Manganese Mine to Get US Approval
item.description: The Trump administration is set to authorize South32 Ltd.’s planned $2 billion zinc and manganese mine in Arizona on Tuesday.

item.title: Carney Cites NATO, Melting Arctic as Germany Wins Submarine Contract
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney stressed the importance of defending against growing threats in the melting Arctic as he picked a German-Norwegian offer to build a new fleet of submarines for Canada’s navy.
